subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to Katheryne at the Inazuma Adventurers' Guild

721670101.text: Your deeds on Seirai Island have been reported to me by Miss Etsuko. You've done very well.

721670102.text: But back on topic, the Guild has received a commission of even greater difficulty than that which you accomplished on Seirai. I wonder if you'd be interested...

721670110.text: The person who commissioned this quest is a Miss Sumida. As for the details, it might be best for you to get them straight from her.

721670111.text: Well then, ad astra abyssosque! I await the completion of your next feat.

721670105.text: ...You'd consider that sort of commission difficult? Hmm, I suppose I should take that into account next time...

721670107.text: Regardless, it's not that sort of commission.

721670201.text: #Ah, hello there. Might you be the illustrious {NICKNAME}?

721670206.text: Alright then. So, tell me, have you ever "obtained the mightiest sword in the village"?

721670207.text: The Harbinger of Dawn counts, I guess?

721670208.text: Yeah, didn't we get that sw{RUBY#[S]Triumphant Harbinger of Dawn that Points Towards Victory}ord from Kaeya that one time?

721670209.text: Hahah, that does sound very strong. Maybe even a bit too deliberately so. Still...

721670210.text: Have you led a life surrounded by beautiful men and ladies?

721670211.text: Well then, did you defeat a giant dragon not long after your story began? Or perhaps, did you get wrapped up in some crisis upon which the survival of a nation hung? Have you ever faced off against "an elite antagonistic force with a numbered ranking scheme"?

721670212.text: Well, I can't say I haven't...

721670213.text: But hang on, what do you mean by "not long after your story began"?

721670214.text: Or are you, perhaps, in fact a traveler from "another world," just like the main character in "Flowers for Princess Fischl"?

721670305.text: ...It's nothing. Since Lady Sumida has recommended you, I have no complaints. Are you ready to go to Tsurumi Island?

721670307.text: Then let us go while the weather remains clement.

721670309.text: Come back once you are, then.

721672301.text: After two round trips, you should know which way to go now.

721672303.text: No need to thank me. These were Lady Sumida's instructions, after all.

721672304.text: Actually, Paimon's kinda interested to know...

721672307.text: I have ferried people and goods to Tsurumi Island, and also to the lands across the ocean.

721672308.text: It makes no difference to me. So long as Lady Sumida asks it of me, I will do it.

721672001.text: Are you ready to head back?

721670403.text: Then let us go while the weather remains clement.

721670501.text: Wow! So this is Tsurumi Island? This...

721670502.text: ...Looks really sad! What's with this huge fog!?

721670505.text: Kama, do you know that... Uh, what is it again?

721672101.text: Huh. Feels like we've gotten our bearings now, huh?

721672102.text: Yup, even though the fog hasn't dissipated yet.

721672103.text: Eh? There's a kid over there...

721672104.text: Do Inazuman kids all run off to deserted islands to play when they've got time on their hands?

721672106.text: Yeah, and let's ask about the thing Miss Sumida asked us to get in the meantime.

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to the mysterious young boy

721670602.text: Uh, I didn't mean to scare you...

721670604.text: And you've got... a little floating girl with you too! That's awesome! I haven't seen any outlanders in soooo long!

721670605.text: Paimon's not a "little girl" or whatever. Paimon's Paimon! And who're you, kiddo?

721670610.text: Uh, either way, the important thing here is...

721670805.text: The Perch looks really happy. I'm sure Kapatcir will be really happy too!

721670810.text: Kapatcir loves to hear me sing. I'll be singing for her during the ceremony!

721670811.text: #{NICKNAME} can sing too! Well, {F#her}{M#his} singing turns Glaze Lilies into Whopperflowers, though.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the destination and talk to Ruu

721670701.text: Let me introduce you to Big Sister Makiri and Big Brother Ipe.

721670704.text: Hmm~ the Perch seems to be in a good state. This year's ceremony should go well.

721670705.text: Oh come on, less talking, more offering.

721670706.text: After all, the Perch is the keystone to the ceremony. This is the tree upon which the Great Thunderbird once descended.

721670707.text: Grandpa Mata said that the maintenance of the Perch indicates our respect and worship towards the Great Thunderbird. If it is damaged...

721670708.text: I know. That said, this year's ceremony leaves a bad taste in my mouth...

721670709.text: And the fact that I'm the only one doing work over here makes it worse!

721670710.text: You know what, I think I get this guy.

721670712.text: Eh~ you're just too reliable, Ipe. What's more, this is my first time making offerings to the Perch.

721670713.text: Yeah, yeah, whatever. Anyway, the next step is to touch the Perch. Then, help me look for feathers around this area.

721670715.text: Eh, didn't Grandpa Mata tell you about it? Part of the process is removing all foreign elements from the Perch.

721670716.text: Basically, the power of the Great Thunderbird will accumulate within the Perch, and it will carry off foreign substances that infiltrate Tsurumi Island in the form of "feathers."

721670717.text: Afterward, the fog will purify those feathers. After all, the fog protects our island, and will not let anything pass through the sacred barrier around us.

721670718.text: That's why we need to find the scattered feathers and bring them back to the Perch.

721670719.text: Oh~ I see, I see. I get it now.

721670722.text: (Big Sister Makiri's just pretending to not get it.)

721670725.text: So we just need to find those feathers, right?

721670726.text: So we just need to find some weird looking feathers.

721670727.text: It's made using the Great Thunderbird's power, so if you have keen elemental senses like Ruu does, finding them would be a cinch.

721670733.text: C'mon, you two. Let's go find those feathers! If you help make offerings to the Perch, I'm sure Kapatcir would be happy.

721670734.text: Uhh... Alright then. Let's just touch that perch first, shall we?

721672201.text: Well, that's all the Perches settled. Guess they can start the ceremony without a hitch now, huh?

721672202.text: Mm-mm, after hearing Ruu talk about it so much, Paimon's getting all excited!

721672208.text: Even if you don't wanna go, we've got to be there if we wanna get that Maushiro.

721672205.text: Eh? But he did say a lot about it! You know, like how excited everyone was and how we were welcome...

subQuests.subQuestName: Make an offering to the Perch

721671004.text: Hmm, looks like there's something over there...

721672502.text: Nice! Guess Ruu didn't trick us after all!

721672503.text: Well, I suppose that's this commission done.

721672505.text: And what were you cheated out of, exactly?

721672506.text: They said there'd be a ceremony! And we helped them out with so many things, too!

721672508.text: True, but there is one thing that's still very strange...

721672511.text: There should've been more people here, but it looks like all of them have vanished...

721672512.text: And all those people felt like they had a few screws loose, anyway...

721672513.text: Whatever. Let's go look for Kama first.

721672514.text: He should be waiting for us at the entrance.

721672510.text: Paimon thinks there's something odd about this place, too...

721670902.text: We're here to take part in the ceremony.

721670903.text: Ah, when will we be ready to hold the ceremony? Preparations for the Perch on Ipe's side should already be complete.

721670904.text: He's there with Makiri, so there shouldn't be any issues.

721670905.text: We've finished making the offerings to the Perch over there!

721670906.text: But there are three more Perches. Who knows how the preparations there are going...

721670907.text: We can go have a look at those.

721670908.text: Where are those three other perches?

721670909.text: I hope that... No, the Great Thunderbird will surely be pleased with the ceremony this time...

721670915.text: Aw, c'mon! Why's he ignoring us?

721672601.text: #Ah, hello there. Might you be the illustrious {NICKNAME}?

721672606.text: Alright then. So, tell me, have you ever "obtained the mightiest sword in the village"?

721672607.text: Have you led a life surrounded by beautiful men and ladies?

721672608.text: Well then, did you defeat a giant dragon not long after your story began? Or perhaps, did you get wrapped up in some crisis upon which the survival of a nation hung? Have you ever faced off against "an elite antagonistic force with a numbered ranking scheme"?

721672609.text: Well, I can't say I haven't...

721672610.text: But hang on, what do you mean by "not long after your story began"?

721672611.text: Or are you, perhaps, in fact a traveler from "another world," just like the main character in "Flowers for Princess Fischl"?

721671303.text: Go through the great gate over there. This used to be one of Tsurumi Island's traditions.

721671304.text: If not, you'll get lost in the fog very easily.

721671404.text: The fog... If it's as Grandpa Mata says, and the fog is so powerful that nothing can invade Tsurumi Island, how do things from the outside get into the Perches?

721671405.text: That's because those foreign substances come from within the ground. The fog can't stop things that come from there, which is why we need to make offerings and purify the Perches.

721671406.text: Huh. And here I thought the fog could do anything.

721671407.text: It's the same for things in the sea. I've fished up some weird stuff before.

721671410.text: When you touch the Perch, the feathers will fly to nearby areas. Afterward, you're going to have to rely on your senses. If you've got a good nose for the elements, this should be easy.

subQuests.subQuestName: Find your way through the mist and make an offering at the Perches

721671701.text: Even if it was only just once, I'd love to leave the Sea of Fog and see what lies beyond...

721671702.text: Are you an idiot? It's utter darkness out there.

721671703.text: Didn't the priest say that if we leave the fog, our souls will become lost shadows that roam the Realm of Silence beyond?

721671704.text: If it wasn't for the Great Thunderbird using the fog to protect the island, we'd have been goners long ago.

721671705.text: I know, and that's why we hold ceremonies to thank the Great Thunderbird for its protection.

721671706.text: ...But aren't you curious about the outside world anyway?

721671707.text: There were those who tried to leave this place and follow the Great Thunderbird's light to seek new lands. None of them returned alive. You do remember the Kama family's boy, don't you, old man?

721671709.text: Perhaps I simply wish that all went well with him...

721671603.text: Have you brought the item that Lady Sumida asked for?

721671608.text: Nothing. I'll send you back now. Are you ready to depart?

721671801.text: Where's that Ruu kid gone off to?

721671802.text: Seriously now. It's almost time, and we can't start without him.

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to Kama and then return

721672401.text: I hope that... No, the Great Thunderbird will surely be pleased with the ceremony this time...

721671102.text: I really hope you've brought the Maushiro this time... Or else...

721671103.text: ...Or else my novel will never get written!

721671104.text: Oh, come on! A commission of this level was a piece of cake for us!

721671105.text: #C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's show her the Maushiro we found!

721671106.text: Let's finish this commission, get paid, and head over to Kiminami Restaurant for a good meal...

721671110.text: That's impossible! We just got it!

721671201.text: You're back. Do you have the Maushiro?

721671203.text: Him? ...Well, it all started when I heard Tang Wen mention Wangshu Inn's Almond Tofu. I thought it would make for a good addition to my novels. For example...

721671204.text: ...Um, I mean. So he's a reliable man who can get you to all sorts of places with eyes. He can even pass through the storms of a sealed nation.

721671205.text: He's got that "keeping his true power a mystery, only to join the protagonist's party in the closing phases of the story" sort of feeling to him, you know? I've worked with him many times.

721671207.text: It is an island to the distant south of Narukami Island, shrouded in a perpetual veil of fog. According to the "Tales of Distant Seas," there were settlements on that island up till several millennia ago, but they were laid waste due to some unknown reason.

721671208.text: Very interesting, no? Uh, I know it's not exactly respectful to say that a civilization's fall is "interesting," but it really does make my writing hand itch! "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog (Working Title)" is meant to be an adventure title set on Tsurumi Island based on what we already know about its culture...

721671211.text: Please find the Maushiro... This year's "This Novel is Amazing!" grand prize is at stake!

721671901.text: Kina, the old mural that we found previously...

721671902.text: Yeah, that's right. That weird round shape, and all those nut-like shapes around it...

721671903.text: I asked Grandpa Mata about them. He told me that this was what the ancient world looked like... before it was swallowed up by the darkness.

721671904.text: To protect Tsurumi Island, the Great Thunderbird created the great Sea of Fog such that even the darkness would lose its way and become unable to enter the island.

721671905.text: ...Yeah, that's cool and all, but what's that got to do with those shapes?

721671906.text: That's so weird, right? Not to mention how the priests on the drawings up there don't look like Grandpa Mata or the others at all.
